turns.note: Start with a moderate C6/C7 split at the feed to recover the valuable heavy products while avoiding very tall, high-reflux equipment. This first run will also establish separation sharpness and cost scale.

I am testing a complete seven-column blend-oriented sequence with a sharper C5/C6 feed split. Higher boil-up should move the residual C5 into the light branch, while downstream columns recover C3/C4/C5 blends, both C6 blends, and pure C7-C9 products.

I interpret the measured failures as cut-point problems rather than a bad topology: sharpen C3/C4, keep heptane out of the C6 branch, split paraffins from naphthenes, and tighten the valuable heptane/octane/nonane cuts. The unchanged root and C5 product preserve the proven $645M/yr blend sale.
Restore the measured valid six-column design that earned 1.088: it sells C3 and C5 blends plus premium n-octane, while avoiding the failed high-severity settings.

I am targeting four valuable unsold pools: depropanize TTB to sell the C4 blend, recover heptane from BBT with a C7/C8 split followed by a cyclohexane/C7 split, and sharpen the octane/nonane cut. The earlier weak BBBB settings left both outlets near 85% purity, so substantially sharper settings are warranted.

I interpret the unsold C4, C7/C8 and C8/C9 pools as the largest near-term opportunities. I am sharpening the C4/C5 cut and adding depropanizing, heptane recovery and octane/nonane columns; the retrieved runs establish the feed compositions and convergence baseline.

The current measured design leaves valuable C4, heptane, and nonane pools unsold. I will test depropanizing TTB for a C4 blend, splitting and polishing BBT for heptane, and sharpening BBBB for octane/nonane recovery.
I am sharpening the three near-sale cuts: BT for a 95% C6-paraffin tops blend, TTB for a 95% C4 bottoms blend, and BBBB to lift nonane above 95% while retaining premium octane.

The measured zero-value outlets contain large recoverable C4, C6, C7 and C8 flows. I am adding targeted splits for those outlets and sharpening the existing C3/C4 and C8/C9 columns; the product values are estimates until simulated.

The measured current flowsheet projects strong revenue but is invalid solely because TTB failed at 90/8/10. I am replacing only that column with a much milder depropanizer to preserve the rest of the profitable plant and obtain a valid C4-blend recovery.

My interpretation is that the zero-value C4 and C6 cuts need sharper fractionation, while the heavy branch can gain both recovery and 99% premiums. I am also deleting BBTTT because its measured $4.4M/yr cost produces no sale.

The measured current run shows four large unsold pools: C4/C5, mixed C6 paraffins/naphthenes, cyclohexane/heptane, and a heptane-contaminated octane bottoms. I am sharpening exactly those cuts; the C4 change also moves more propane overhead at TT so the downstream C4 stream can reach blend purity.

Measured fact: four currently unsold streams contain recoverable C3/C4, C7/cyclohexane, and C7/C8 pools. I am testing relatively easy boiling-point splits on those pools while leaving all profitable upstream columns unchanged.

Measured facts: both BTB outlets are unsold despite its $51.9M/yr cost, while several small C4/C5 and C7/C8 outlets fall just below sale purity and the octane products are only 96–97% pure. My interpretation is that pruning BTB and sharpening these easier splits should add revenue and premium-grade value at modest incremental cost.

Measured: TTBT is the only failed column and has no saleable outlet; BTB and TTBBB are unsold pools containing valuable C6 and butane. Interpretation: removing TTBT secures validity and saves cost, while moderate sharp splits on BTB and TTBBB may recover paraffin/naphthene blends and additional n-butane.

I am testing a sharper propane/C4 split followed by C4/C5 recovery, while removing the low-value butane polishing chain. I am also strengthening the two close C6 separations to target saleable hexane, naphthene blend, and cyclohexane rather than zero-value mixed outlets.

Return to the best measured design, then test a sharper depropanizer to make the C4 blend saleable. Remove the C6 paraffin/naphthene splitter because its measured outlets were both unsaleable, so deleting it should preserve revenue while avoiding its cost.

The measured best design has five unsold streams with valuable, separable components. I am adding small downstream columns to recover the two C6 blends from BTB, C3/C4 products from TTBT, cyclohexane from BBTTTT, heptane/octane from BBTBBT, and the C5 blend from TTBBBB.
Remove the failed propane/isobutane splitter and two downstream splitters whose measured outlets earn nothing. This should restore validity and cut cost without sacrificing measured revenue.

Measured: BTB is a 460 mol/s unsold paraffin/naphthene mixture, TTBT is a 190 mol/s unsold C3/C4 mixture, and BBTTTT is a 48 mol/s unsold cyclohexane-rich stream. Hypothesis: three sharp splits will create saleable C6 paraffin and naphthene blends, C3/C4 blends, and cyclohexane with attractive revenue relative to their column costs.
I am restoring convergence with moderate depropanizer settings and removing two measured zero-revenue subtrees; this should preserve all saleable products while cutting cost.

The measured flowsheet leaves a large C6 paraffin/naphthene pool unsold and a smaller cyclohexane pool unsold; I am adding splits to monetize both. I am also modestly sharpening the propane/C4 cut, which is only about two percentage points short of blend purity.

The measured BTB outlets are both unsold despite containing valuable C6 paraffin and naphthene pools. I am shifting the cut toward the n-hexane/methylcyclopentane boundary with more boil-up and sharper fractionation, aiming to sell both as blends; BBTTTT is pruned because both measured outlets are worthless.

Restore the best design, which avoids the zero-value BTB separation cost. Test two targeted purity upgrades: premium octane at BBBT and saleable cyclohexane at BBTTTT, while retaining the valuable heptane and nonane products.

Target the three largest unsold recoverable fractions: split the isobutane/N-butane residue, sharpen cyclohexane recovery, and push the 94% octane stream above sale purity. These are local changes, so unchanged upstream columns should not consume additional solves.

The measured unsold BTB stream contains about 216 mol/s n-hexane and 162 mol/s C6 naphthenes, while BBTTTT contains about 38 mol/s cyclohexane and TTBTBT about 36 mol/s isobutane. I am testing three targeted recovery columns; their purity gains and costs remain hypotheses until simulated.
Prune the two measured zero-revenue subtrees. This preserves every saleable product while eliminating $51.5M/yr of column cost.

The measured BTB stream is unsold but contains about 216 mol/s n-hexane and 160 mol/s C6 naphthenes. I interpret a sharp n-hexane/methylcyclopentane cut as capable of producing both a C6-paraffin blend and a C6-naphthene blend, converting this large waste pool into revenue.

Restore the best measured design, which avoids the unprofitable BTB separation. I am testing two small, high-value finishing columns: cyclohexane purification from BBTTTT and a sharper propane/isobutane split at TTBTBT; their modest feed rates should keep incremental cost low.

The measured BTB stream contains about 350 mol/s of C6 paraffins and 160 mol/s of C6 naphthenes but is unsold. I am adding a sharp paraffin/naphthene split; both outlets should qualify as blends and recover substantial value.
Return to the best measured design before spending the remaining solves; the current additions include zero-revenue subtrees whose costs explain the drop from the best reward.

I interpret both unsold streams as recoverable C6-naphthene pools: BTB should yield a naphthene-rich bottoms blend, while BBTTTT only needs heptane rejection to qualify its tops. I am testing moderate columns sized to those cuts.

Prune the measured zero-value BTB branch, then test sharper cyclohexane recovery from BBTTTT and fuller isobutane recovery from TTBTBTT; both feeds already contain concentrated valuable product but current cuts discard substantial material.
